inventory.goal: Opit, että funktio antaa jokaiselle syötteelle täsmälleen yhden arvon, ja osaat laskea arvon f(x).
inventory.intro: Funktio on kone: jokaiselle syötteelle se antaa täsmälleen yhden arvon.

demos.say: Kone kertoo kahdella ja lisää yhden. Syötteet kulkevat koneen läpi, ja taulukko täyttyy. Syöte 3 tulee kahdesti, ja molemmilla kerroilla arvo on 7.
demos.label: funktiokone
demos.finalCaption: Sama syöte antoi saman arvon. Jokaisella syötteellä on täsmälleen yksi arvo.

demos.say: Tämä kone on oikukas: syöte 2 antaa ensin 4, sitten 5. Kun yksi syöte antaa kaksi eri arvoa, kone ei ole funktio.
demos.label: rikkinäinen kone
demos.finalCaption: Syöte 2 antoi kaksi eri arvoa. Funktio ei saa tehdä niin.

demos.say: Funktiota merkitään f(x) = 2x + 1. Silloin f(3) tarkoittaa arvoa, joka tulee syötteellä 3: f(3) = 7.

isFunc.hint: Etsi syöte, joka esiintyy kahdesti. Onko sillä sama arvo?
isFunc.explain: Jokaisella syötteellä on täsmälleen yksi arvo: funktio.

pairs.hint: Ratkaisevaa on, antaako sama syöte eri arvoja. Sama arvo eri syötteille on sallittu.
pairs.explain: Funktio: yksi syöte → yksi arvo. Sama arvo saa toistua, mutta sama syöte ei saa antaa kahta eri arvoa.

run.hint: Kerro ensin, lisää tai vähennä sitten.

alignment.comparison: Retain actual run/rule/isFunc/pairs/transfer inventory and three demos. Inherit repeated-input same-output check and allow many-to-one. Main conceptual construction avoids arithmetic prerequisites attached broadly to every Lite family. Optional f(x) example separately marks EXPR-EVAL. Correct finite evidence/black-box ambiguity, define entire finite domain and include missing-value boundary; COVERAGE misses pairs/sort and third demo.
reconciliationForOpus: COVERAGE omits pairs/sort and third f(x) demo.

Every given-input-one-value record is a finite table compatible with a function; a few repeated black-box tests do not establish unrestricted behavior. State the full finite domain for definitive checks.
Whole-lesson arithmetic assumptions in registry exceed isFunc/pairs concept demand. Main finite mapping construction supplies no calculation prerequisite; optional arithmetic is separate.
Retain many-to-one and repeated-identical-row cases; do not mistake a repeated output or identical observation for a conflict.

planning.evidenceLimits: All plans, numerical bounds, contexts and controls are project design. Canonical concept/atomic role retained. No practice recognition/choice is described as free construction or independent long-term understanding; no human efficacy claim.

interaction.action: 3×3 native toggle buttons for arrows, each row labelled input and buttons explicitly output. Start repair board0→2,1→2 plus1→1, input2 missing. Add/remove arrows freely; drawn mapping and text summary synchronise. Check accepts any of27 complete single-valued maps, not only the original example. No drag or arbitrary naming.
interaction.checkedMeaning: Specific feedback names a permitted input with zero outputs or multiple distinct outputs. Correct confirms only that this complete finite mapping satisfies the property, not rule inference/every possible integer. Test-input view may inspect a row; this is observation support.
interaction.domain: Dense records of canonical finite input/output pairs. Validate every own required index, tuple shape and finite in-domain values before relation logic. Repeated identical observations do not break mathematical single-valuedness; toggling UI keeps a set of arrows. Empty stated domain not used in this lesson. Extra unknown domain/output values reject.
interaction.feedback: Arrow insertion/deletion invalidates the mapping verdict. Selecting which input to inspect and optional help leave it valid because the relation is unchanged. The domain remains fixed at0,1,2; no domain-change or row-order control is claimed.
tests: Enumerate all512 subsets of3×3 arrows; exactly27 satisfy one output for every0,1,2.
Accept all-to2 and other many-to-one maps, unused output and duplicate identical observation; reject same input with different outputs.
Reject missing one input, extra out-of-domain input, malformed tuples, undefined/holes/inherited-only index, NaN/Infinity and prototype-name tokens.
Changing only viewed input or row display order keeps a global mapping verdict. The domain is fixed; foreign input values are rejected by the checker rather than changing it.
Repeated observed pairs on a finite table never prove an unbounded black box is a function. Pause/reset/dispose/remount and actual accessible labels/44px UI.
